minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  April 23, 2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Mayor
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Eric Podley, BUSD
  Vanessa Hess, BHS Student Rep.
  Mike Gaydos, BHS Student Rep.
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Krista Chakmak, Resident
  Kim Svatos, Resident
  Matt Svatos, Resident
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Sara Rodriguez, Tri-City
  Elsa Matsumoto, Tri-City
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the March meeting were approved.

4. Summer Lunch Program  Bill Aguirre with the City of La Verne provided an
  overview of the upcoming Summer Lunch Program.
  The program will begin on June 10th and will go
  through August 16th this year. As in previous years,
  the City will be providing a recreation component to
  go along with the lunches.

  JR Ranells with the City of La Verne noted that the
  group had previously shared interest in doing a video
  advertising the Summer Lunch Program. The group
  further discussed the program’s outreach efforts and
  possible opportunities to expand with partnerships.
  Additionally, this year’s program will continue to
  include visits by the Community Navigator and the
  Police Department will review the possibility of
  distributing school supplies donated through the
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes April 23, 2019, page 2

  Stuff-a-Squad car program. After no further
  discussion, the group provided staff direction to
  complete a video informing the community of the
  program as well as requesting donations to support
  it.

5. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  noted that things at the schools had been going well.
  He credited the administration and faculty for being
  proactive with their efforts and training. The group
  was also very pleased to hear that SRO Cambero
  would be returning as the SRO next school year.

6. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with BUSD provided a report on school
  district items including an update on the expansion of
  counseling services in La Verne schools. Mark also
  noted that testing has been taking place and that
  district staff will be moving back into the revamped
  offices in San Dimas soon.

7. School Counseling  David Yim with Tri-City Mental Health Services
  provided the March 2019 School Counseling Report.
  Visits with students contain the same subject matters
  including depressive symptoms, poor behaviors, family
  issues, anxiety, and grief/loss. Students receiving
  services have shown improvement in their behavior at
  the schools which is a positive sign of the program’s
  success. Some recent challenges are related to
  shortages in office space to meet with students as a
  result of the unusually rainy season. Normally, outside
  spaces are used to meet with students but with a
  number of days experiencing inclement weather,
  finding meeting space has been more difficult.

  Mike Gaydos with Bonita High School noted that the
  program has had positive benefits to students and
  complimented YFAC for continuing their support.

8. Youth of the Year  Mayor Kendrick reported on the creation of the Youth
  of the Year Award and how the YFAC Executive
  Committee became involved as the selecting body.
  The award is based off of nominations from the
  community and this year’s selection was YFAC
  member and Bonita High School Representative
  Vanessa Hess. Vanessa’s recognition is well
  deserved. Her participation has been a great help to
  YFAC by ensuring that programs and discussions
  include a youth perspective.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes April 23, 2019, page 3

9. Therapeutic Garden  Sara Rodriguez and Elsa Matsumoto from Tri-City
  Mental Health’s Therapeutic Community Garden
  provided a report on their recent activities. The garden
  helps to nurture wellness through spiritual, mental, and
  physical health. The garden is open to community
  members and tours are available.

10. Round Table  Hollie Savage of the Police Department noted that the
  recent Tip-a-Cop fundraiser held at Mi Ranchito
  supporting the Special Olympics raised $2,300. The
  next fundraiser will be held April 30th at Lordsburg
  Taphouse. Hollie also provided information on the
  associated upcoming Torch Run and the Police
  Department sponsored Drug Take Back Day being
  held on April 27th.

  SRO Cambero shared a personal story on mental
  health impacts in law enforcement.

  David Yim shared information on the recent 88 Cities
  feature in the LA Times that shared information about
  La Verne.

  Eric Podley provided updates on the construction
  taking place at the high school.

  Mike Gaydos noted the importance of being aware of
  what programs are available and being able to remove
  the stigma associated with utilizing those services. He
  also shared that he will be attending American Legion
  Boys State.

  Vanessa Hess reported to the group that she had
  been accepted to UC Irvine and will be doing
  fundraising events to help with expenses. Her first
  effort will be a yard sale on May 4th.

  Krista Chakmak inquired about the upcoming
  Recreation Guide.

  JR Ranells noted that Denim Day which provides
  sexual assault victim awareness would be taking place
  the next day.

  Council Member Robin Carder gave compliments to
  the school district, Tri-City’s, and the Police
  Department for all they do for the community.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes April 23, 2019, page 4

11.  Next Meeting  The group discussed the reasons for not having a
  meeting in May and determined that a May meeting
  will be held. The next YFAC meeting is scheduled
  for May 28, 2019 at 6:30 p.m.

12. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:40 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
